question: Should OpenClaw standardize signed installation or agent-profile identity for selected external requests, and exactly which request families may emit it?
rationale: Current behavior is intentionally narrower, while the general proposal requires human judgment about claim meaning, trust roots, key ownership, privacy, replay, redirects, and core-versus-plugin ownership.

options.title: Define truthful signed identity
options.body: Specify an audience-bound installation or agent-profile assertion with explicit limitations and complete security semantics before implementation.

options.title: Use plugin-specific authentication
options.body: Keep service credentials and request signing in plugin-owned tools unless a concrete missing generic plugin API is demonstrated.

options.title: Decline general attestation
options.body: Retain provider attribution and document that OpenClaw cannot prove autonomous-agent initiation.

recommendation.title: Define truthful signed identity
recommendation.body: Specify an audience-bound installation or agent-profile assertion with explicit limitations and complete security semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the closest shipped attribution behavior and provided the existing product/security direction on this tracker.
